title: MITRE ATT&CK T1046: Network Service Discovery
text:
Technique ID: T1046 - Network Service Discovery
Tactics: discovery, reconnaissance
Platforms: linux, windows, network, macos
Description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including port scanning (e.g. TCP SYN scan, vertical port sweeps) to identify listening services and potential vulnerabilities.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1030: Network Traffic Filtering - Configure stateful firewall rules to block unsolicited scanning traffic and rate-limit SYN packets.
- M1031: Network Intrusion Prevention - Deploy NIDS/NIPS with signatures for sequential and distributed port sweep anomalies.
- M1038: Execution Prevention - Disable unneeded external daemons and bind sensitive management ports to localhost.

Detection Guidance:
Monitor network flows (NetFlow/IPFIX) and firewall logs for high volume of SYN packets or connections across multiple destination ports in a short duration.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1046: Network Service Discovery

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1110.001: Brute Force: Password Guessing
text:
Technique ID: T1110.001 - Brute Force: Password Guessing
Tactics: credential_access
Platforms: linux, windows, macos, cloud, saas
Description: Adversaries may systematically guess passwords to authenticate to user accounts on single hosts or services like SSH, RDP, or web portals.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1036: Account Use Policies - Implement account lockouts or exponential authentication delays (e.g., fail2ban) after repeated failed attempts.
- M1032: Multi-Factor Authentication - Mandate hardware security keys or TOTP MFA for all interactive and remote sessions.
- M1027: Password Policies - Enforce robust password length and complexity requirements.

Detection Guidance:
Correlate authentication failures (Event ID 4625 on Windows, 'Failed password' in /var/log/auth.log) from a single source host or account within brief sliding windows.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1110.001: Brute Force: Password Guessing

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1110.003: Brute Force: Password Spraying
text:
Technique ID: T1110.003 - Brute Force: Password Spraying
Tactics: credential_access
Platforms: linux, windows, macos, cloud, saas
Description: Adversaries may attempt a small number of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to avoid account lockout thresholds.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1032: Multi-Factor Authentication - Enforce modern MFA mechanisms across all single sign-on (SSO) and LDAP endpoints.
- M1036: Account Use Policies - Monitor distributed authentication patterns across multiple accounts originating from identical ASN or IP subnets.
- M1017: User Training - Educate users on credential exposure and common dictionary passwords.

Detection Guidance:
Track failed logon events across multiple distinct usernames originating from a single IP address or subnet over a 5 to 15 minute window.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1110.003: Brute Force: Password Spraying

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1078: Valid Accounts
text:
Technique ID: T1078 - Valid Accounts
Tactics: defense_evasion, persistence, privilege_escalation, initial_access
Platforms: linux, windows, macos, cloud, network
Description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1015: Privileged Account Management - Restrict privileged accounts from interactive logons on standard workstations.
- M1026: Privileged Process Integrity - Implement Just-In-Time (JIT) access and ephemeral credentials.
- M1032: Multi-Factor Authentication - Require phishing-resistant MFA on all administrative interfaces.

Detection Guidance:
Identify anomalous logins following failed brute-force bursts, unexpected geolocation shifts, or off-hours administrative access.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1078: Valid Accounts

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1548.003: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
text:
Technique ID: T1548.003 - Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
Tactics: privilege_escalation, defense_evasion
Platforms: linux, macos
Description: Adversaries may execute commands with sudo rights or abuse misconfigured sudoers files and cached credentials to elevate to root.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1026: Privileged Process Integrity - Configure sudoers to require explicit re-authentication (timestamp_timeout=0) and avoid wildcard NOPASSWD entries.
- M1022: Restrict File and Directory Permissions - Restrict write permissions to /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d/ to root only.
- M1028: Operating System Configuration - Enforce least privilege and remove unneeded users from the sudo/wheel groups.

Detection Guidance:
Monitor syslog and auditd for 'COMMAND=' executions with sudo by accounts not belonging to authorized system administration groups.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1548.003: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1136.001: Create Account: Local Account
text:
Technique ID: T1136.001 - Create Account: Local Account
Tactics: persistence
Platforms: linux, windows, macos
Description: Adversaries may create a local account to maintain access to victim systems without needing to maintain active malware payloads.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1018: User Account Management - Audit user creation events and automatically alert on new accounts created outside central IAM workflows.
- M1026: Privileged Process Integrity - Limit useradd, adduser, and net user execution rights to authorized orchestration agents.
- M1028: Operating System Configuration - Regularly audit /etc/passwd and SAM databases for unauthorized accounts.

Detection Guidance:
Detect useradd/adduser in Linux syslog or Windows Event ID 4720 (A user account was created) that lack associated service desk tickets.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1136.001: Create Account: Local Account

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1595.003: Active Scanning: Wordlist Scanning
text:
Technique ID: T1595.003 - Active Scanning: Wordlist Scanning
Tactics: reconnaissance
Platforms: network, web
Description: Adversaries may probe web servers using dictionary lists of paths (e.g., /admin, /.git, /.env, /config) to discover unlinked or sensitive directories.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1021: Restrict Web-Based Content - Disable public access to hidden directories, dotfiles, and administration portals.
- M1050: Exploit Protection - Implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) configured to rate limit and ban IPs scanning non-existent paths.
- M1030: Network Traffic Filtering - Restrict administrative interfaces to internal corporate VPNs.

Detection Guidance:
Look for high frequencies of HTTP 404, 401, or 403 status codes in web server access logs targeting sensitive URLs.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1595.003: Active Scanning: Wordlist Scanning

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059.004: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
text:
Technique ID: T1059.004 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
Tactics: execution
Platforms: linux, macos
Description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shells (bash, sh, zsh) to execute arbitrary commands, download secondary payloads, and chain lateral attacks.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1038: Execution Prevention - Restrict execution of interactive shells by unprivileged service daemons (e.g. www-data).
- M1026: Privileged Process Integrity - Deploy process whitelisting via AppArmor or SELinux.
- M1047: Audit - Enable Linux auditd execve logging.

Detection Guidance:
Detect abnormal parent-child process relationships, such as apache/nginx or python spawning /bin/sh or /bin/bash.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059.004: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.004: Remote Services: SSH
text:
Technique ID: T1021.004 - Remote Services: SSH
Tactics: lateral_movement
Platforms: linux, macos
Description: Adversaries may log in to remote machines using SSH with stolen credentials or hijacked SSH keys to move laterally across an internal subnet.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1035: Limit Access to Resource over Network - Segment management networks and restrict SSH access to jump hosts/bastions.
- M1032: Multi-Factor Authentication - Require hardware MFA for all SSH sessions.
- M1027: Password Policies - Disable password-based SSH authentication in favor of ed25519 public keys.

Detection Guidance:
Alert on east-west SSH connections between non-bastion workstations or unusual jump sequences across production tiers.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.004: Remote Services: SSH

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1486: Data Encrypted for Impact
text:
Technique ID: T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact
Tactics: impact
Platforms: linux, windows, macos
Description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems or attached network storage to disrupt system availability and demand ransom.

Remediation & Mitigations:
- M1053: Data Backup - Maintain immutable, air-gapped backups of critical systems and test restore procedures regularly.
- M1022: Restrict File and Directory Permissions - Enforce strict write and execute access controls on shared storage and databases.
- M1040: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint - Deploy EDR with automated anti-ransomware heuristic file-modification blocks.

Detection Guidance:
Monitor for rapid file modification/rename operations, deletion of volume shadow copies (vssadmin), or bulk creation of ransom notes.

provenance.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1486: Data Encrypted for Impact

title: OWASP Top 10:2021-A01 Broken Access Control
text:
OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control.
Description: Access control enforces policy such that users cannot act outside of their intended permissions. Failures typically lead to unauthorized information disclosure, modification, or destruction of all data, or performing a business function outside the user's limits.
Key Vulnerabilities: Bypassing access control checks by modifying the URL, internal application state, or the HTML page, or using a custom API attack tool; permitting viewing or editing someone else's account by providing its unique identifier (IDOR).
Remediation & ASVS V4 Verification:
- Enforce least privilege by default. Deny all access except for public resources.
- Implement access control checks server-side in trusted business logic components.
- Disable web server directory listing and ensure file metadata (e.g. .git, .env) is not present within web roots.
- Rate limit API and controller access to minimize the harm from automated brute-forcing or scanning tools.

provenance.title: OWASP Top 10:2021-A01 Broken Access Control

title: OWASP Top 10:2021-A02 Cryptographic Failures
text:
OWASP A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures (formerly Sensitive Data Exposure).
Description: Transmitting data in clear text (HTTP, SMTP, FTP, Telnet) or using weak cryptographic protocols and outdated ciphers exposes sensitive secrets, tokens, and session identifiers to network eavesdropping.
Remediation & ASVS V9 Verification:
- Classify data processed, stored, or transmitted by an application. Identify sensitive data per privacy laws.
- Encrypt all sensitive data in transit with secure TLS (TLS 1.3 or 1.2 with modern AEAD cipher suites).
- Disable deprecated protocols including Telnet (port 23), FTP (port 21), and cleartext HTTP (port 80).
- Enforce HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) with long max-age and includeSubDomains directives.

provenance.title: OWASP Top 10:2021-A02 Cryptographic Failures

title: OWASP Top 10:2021-A07 Identification and Authentication Failures
text:
OWASP A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures.
Description: Confirmation of the user's identity, authentication, and session management is critical to protect against authentication-related attacks such as credential stuffing, brute force, and stolen session token replays.
Remediation & ASVS V2 Verification:
- Where possible, implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) to prevent automated credential stuffing and brute force.
- Do not deploy with default credentials, particularly for administrator accounts.
- Implement weak-password checks, such as testing new or changed passwords against the top 10,000 worst passwords list.
- Align password length, complexity, and rotation requirements with NIST SP 800-63B guidelines.
- Limit or increasingly delay failed login attempts (exponential backoff / fail2ban rate limiting).

provenance.title: OWASP Top 10:2021-A07 Identification and Authentication Failures

title: OWASP ASVS v4.0.3 Chapter 5: Validation, Sanitization and Encoding
text:
OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS) Chapter 5.
Scope: Input validation and output encoding architecture to prevent path traversal, code injection, and fuzzing exploits.
Verification Requirements:
- V5.1: Verify that input validation is enforced on a trusted service tier before processing requests.
- V5.2: Verify that path sanitization prevents directory traversal attacks (dot-dot-slash) when accessing filesystem resources.
- V5.3: Verify that all untrusted parameters originating from HTTP headers, URIs, and payloads are sanitized before logging or presentation.
- V5.5: Verify that Web Application Firewall (WAF) inspects payload content-type and rejects unwhitelisted structures.

provenance.title: OWASP ASVS v4.0.3 Chapter 5: Validation, Sanitization and Encoding

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Incident Preparation & Incident Response Policy
text:
NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 Phase 1: Incident Preparation.
Summary: Preparation involves establishing and training an incident response team, acquiring necessary tools and resources, and preventing incidents by ensuring networks, systems, and applications are sufficiently secure.
Key Directives:
- Establish an incident response capability and clear escalation hierarchy.
- Conduct periodic risk assessments on mission-critical assets.
- Maintain an up-to-date asset inventory and contact information for asset owners.
- Deploy centralized, tamper-resistant log aggregation with NTP synchronization.
- Pre-stage digital forensics jump bags and memory acquisition tools.

provenance.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Incident Preparation & Incident Response Policy

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Detection and Analysis Phase
text:
NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 Phase 2: Detection and Analysis.
Summary: Organizations must be prepared to handle incidents that occur despite preventative measures. Early detection enables faster containment and mitigates business disruption.
Core Procedures:
- Profile baseline network traffic patterns and authentication frequencies to detect anomalies.
- Correlate events across heterogeneous sources (network flows, host syslogs, authentication logs).
- Maintain an evidence log documenting every action taken during investigation for chain-of-custody.
- Perform initial severity assessment based on functional impact, information impact, and recoverability effort.

provenance.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Detection and Analysis Phase

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Containment, Eradication, and Recovery Phase
text:
NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 Phase 3: Containment, Eradication, and Recovery.
Summary: Containment prevents the incident from expanding and causing additional damage. Eradication removes components of the incident from the environment, and Recovery restores systems to normal operation.
Execution Steps:
- Select containment strategy (e.g., immediate network isolation, null-routing offending IPs, credential revocation).
- Eradicate attacker persistence: delete unauthorized accounts, remove backdoor cron jobs/services, close vulnerable ports.
- Rebuild compromised systems from trusted baseline images or restore clean backups.
- Implement enhanced logging and continuous perimeter monitoring to ensure the threat actor does not regain foothold.

provenance.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Containment, Eradication, and Recovery Phase

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Post-Incident Activity & Lessons Learned
text:
NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 Phase 4: Post-Incident Activity.
Summary: Organizations should evolve their security posture by analyzing incidents and learning lessons.
Action Items:
- Hold a post-incident 'lessons learned' meeting within two weeks of incident closure.
- Document total business downtime, root causes, detection gaps, and response bottlenecks.
- Update detection rules and automated correlation logic to prevent recurrent intrusions.
- Preserve evidence retention per legal and regulatory compliance guidelines.

provenance.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Post-Incident Activity & Lessons Learned

title: CIS Control 4: Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software
text:
CIS Control 4: Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software.
Overview: Establish and maintain the secure configuration of enterprise assets (workstations, servers, network devices) and software (operating systems and applications).
Key Safeguards:
- 4.1: Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process.
- 4.3: Configure Automatic Session Locking on Enterprise Assets.
- 4.7: Manage Default Accounts on Enterprise Assets and Software (change or disable default administrative credentials).
- 4.8: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets.
- Sudo Hardening: Require password re-entry, forbid NOPASSWD for privileged binaries, and maintain immutable audit logs.

title: CIS Control 5: Account Management
text:
CIS Control 5: Account Management.
Overview: Use processes and tools to assign, manage, verify, revoke, and audit credentials and privileges for user, administrator, and service accounts for enterprise assets and software.
Key Safeguards:
- 5.1: Maintain an Inventory of Accounts.
- 5.2: Use Unique Passwords and Mandate Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
- 5.3: Disable Dormant and Inactive Accounts after 45 days.
- 5.4: Restrict Administrator Privileges to Dedicated Administrative Accounts.
- 5.5: Establish and Follow an Automated Account De-provisioning Workflow.

title: CIS Control 6: Access Control Management
text:
CIS Control 6: Access Control Management.
Overview: Use processes and tools to create, assign, manage, and revoke access credentials and privileges for user, administrator, and service accounts over network resources and data assets.
Key Safeguards:
- 6.1: Establish an Access Granting Process based on least privilege and need-to-know.
- 6.2: Establish an Access Revoking Process for departing employees within 24 hours.
- 6.3: Require MFA for Externally-Exposed and Remote Access Systems (SSH bastions, VPNs, web admin portals).
- 6.7: Centralize Access Control via Enterprise IAM / Active Directory.

title: CIS Control 17: Incident Response Management
text:
CIS Control 17: Incident Response Management.
Overview: Establish a program to develop and maintain an incident response capability (e.g. policies, plans, roles, training) to quickly detect attacks and contain, eradicate, and restore systems.
Key Safeguards:
- 17.1: Designate Personnel to Manage Incident Handling.
- 17.2: Establish and Maintain Contact Information for Reporting Security Incidents.
- 17.3: Establish and Maintain an Enterprise Incident Handling Process.

title: Incident Playbook: SSH Brute Force and Credential Stuffing Remediation
text:
# Playbook IR-PB-01: SSH Brute Force & Credential Access Containment

## 1. Triage & Assessment
- Verify whether source IP is an internal scanner or external malicious adversary.
- Check if any failed attempts were followed by an 'Accepted password' or 'Accepted publickey' event.

## 2. Containment Actions
- Immediate Network Isolation: Insert firewall rule dropping all incoming packets from the offending source IP at edge router.
- Fail2ban / Dynamic Jails: Ensure automated ban jail is activated with minimum 24-hour retention.
- If successful login occurred: Immediately terminate active user sessions (`pkill -u <username> -9`) and lock the account.

## 3. Eradication & Recovery
- Force credential rotation for targeted accounts across all corporate SSO endpoints.
- Disable password authentication in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (`PasswordAuthentication no`). Mandate ed25519 keys.

provenance.title: Incident Playbook: SSH Brute Force and Credential Stuffing Remediation

title: Incident Playbook: Network Service Scanning & Reconnaissance Containment
text:
# Playbook IR-PB-02: Network Service Scanning & Port Sweep Containment

## 1. Triage & Assessment
- Determine scope: Vertical scan (single host, many ports) or Horizontal scan (many hosts, single port).
- Evaluate criticality of scanned destination assets against asset inventory catalog.

## 2. Containment Actions
- Perimeter Filtering: Add null route (blackhole) or stateful ACL drop for source IP.
- Rate Limiting: Apply SYN flood protections and connection rate thresholds on perimeter firewalls.

## 3. Eradication & Hardening
- Audit exposed services on scanned hosts; shut down unnecessary listener ports and daemons.
- Verify internal firewall zoning: Ensure database and management subnets are isolated from public ingress.

provenance.title: Incident Playbook: Network Service Scanning & Reconnaissance Containment

title: Incident Playbook: Unauthorized Sudo and Privilege Escalation Containment
text:
# Playbook IR-PB-03: Unauthorized Privilege Escalation Remediation

## 1. Triage & Assessment
- Identify the executing user and whether they hold authorized administrative role in identity catalog.
- Inspect executed command line, arguments, and parent process tree via auditd.

## 2. Immediate Containment
- Terminate unauthorized active shell sessions spawned via sudo or su (`kill -9 <pid>`).
- Revoke user's sudo access immediately: Remove user from `/etc/sudoers` and `/etc/sudoers.d/`.
- Suspend user login credentials pending incident review.

## 3. Forensics & Eradication
- Audit `/root/.bash_history` and `/tmp` for dropped binaries, scripts, or reverse shells.
- Review Linux audit logs (`ausearch -m USER_CMD -ts today`) for chronological action reconstruction.

provenance.title: Incident Playbook: Unauthorized Sudo and Privilege Escalation Containment

title: Incident Playbook: Rogue Account Creation and Persistence Remediation
text:
# Playbook IR-PB-04: Rogue Account Creation & Persistence Containment

## 1. Triage & Assessment
- Compare newly created account against corporate HR and identity catalogs.
- Check account creation timestamp and correlate with preceding authentication/privilege alerts.

## 2. Immediate Containment
- Lock and delete rogue account: `userdel -r <rogue_user>` (Linux) or `Disable-LocalUser` (Windows).
- Invalidate all active sessions, tokens, and Kerberos tickets for the host.

## 3. Persistence Eradication
- Inspect all user home directories for rogue `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` additions.
- Audit `/etc/cron.*`, `/var/spool/cron`, and systemd service units for unauthorized tasks.
- On Windows, verify scheduled tasks (`schtasks /query`) and registry Run keys.

provenance.title: Incident Playbook: Rogue Account Creation and Persistence Remediation

title: Incident Playbook: Web Application Vulnerability Exploitation & Scanning
text:
# Playbook IR-PB-05: Web Application Fuzzing and Path Exploitation Containment

## 1. Triage & Assessment
- Analyze web server access logs for targeted probes (e.g., `/.env`, `/.git`, `/wp-admin`, SQLi/SSRF payloads).
- Review response codes: determine if requests returned 404/403 (blocked) or 200/500 (potential compromise).

## 2. Containment Actions
- Deploy WAF IP block rule targeting scanner origin IP.
- Apply virtual patch in reverse proxy (Nginx/Apache/Cloudflare) rejecting dotfile and admin path probes.

## 3. Eradication & Hardening
- Ensure sensitive environment files (.env, config.json) are stored outside web server document root.
- Restrict internal administrative consoles to dedicated management subnets or VPN gateways.

provenance.title: Incident Playbook: Web Application Vulnerability Exploitation & Scanning

title: Deloitte Cyber Incident Response Framework (CIRF) & Threat Hunting Guidelines
text:
Deloitte Cyber Incident Response Framework (CIRF) Methodology Summary.
Source URL: https://www.deloitte.com/global/en/services/risk-advisory/services/cyber-incident-response.html

Paraphrased Architecture Notes:
- Rapid Incident Triage: Establishes a unified incident commander model to categorize operational vs systemic threat exposures. Prioritizes containment speed over exhaustive data collection when active lateral movement is observed.
- Proactive Hypothesis-Driven Threat Hunting: Cross-examines telemetry against threat intelligence feeds, assuming the adversary already holds persistence. Scans for beaconing cadences, irregular service creations, and abnormal east-west traffic.
- Forensic Chain of Custody & Evidence Sequestration: Mandates non-destructive volatile memory capture prior to host reboots and bit-stream disk imaging for high-criticality assets.
- Enterprise Resilience & Root-Cause Elimination: Post-containment audits focus on identity perimeter defense, privileged account governance, and closing the initial infection vector before bringing systems back online.

provenance.title: Deloitte Cyber Incident Response Framework (CIRF) & Threat Hunting Guidelines

title: EY Threat Intelligence-Led Incident Response & Containment Methodology
text:
EY Cyber Threat Intelligence-Led Incident Response Methodology Summary.
Source URL: https://www.ey.com/en_gl/services/cybersecurity/incident-response

Paraphrased Architecture Notes:
- Intelligence Integration: Combines MITRE ATT&CK tactic mapping with external adversary profile indicators to anticipate the next phase of an active attack campaign rather than reacting solely to localized alarms.
- Tiered Containment Strategy: Deploys containment measures across micro-segmented network boundaries. Separates infected tenant environments using dynamic firewall policies while preserving operational continuity for unaffected business divisions.
- Identity-First Remediation: Assumes compromised credentials represent the primary vector for persistent re-entry. Enforces coordinated enterprise-wide credential resets, token invalidation, and session termination across federated identity providers.
- Executive Incident Governance: Aligns technical containment milestones with regulatory reporting timelines (e.g. SEC, GDPR, NIS2) to ensure compliance obligations are met during active handling.

provenance.title: EY Threat Intelligence-Led Incident Response & Containment Methodology

title: PwC Incident Management, Digital Forensics & Crisis Remediation Framework
text:
PwC Incident Management and Digital Forensics Framework Summary.
Source URL: https://www.pwc.com/gx/en/services/consulting/cybersecurity-privacy/incident-response.html

Paraphrased Architecture Notes:
- Scalable Crisis Triage: Classifies incidents using a standardized severity matrix balancing operational downtime, data sensitivity, and legal exposure. Directly feeds technical triage findings into business risk registers.
- Deep-Dive Forensic Reconstruction: Employs timeline analysis across multiple log fabrics (host event logs, network proxies, SIEM alerts) to identify the initial compromise timestamp ('patient zero') and map out all secondary compromised nodes.
- Coordinated Mass Eradication: Executes containment and eradication scripts simultaneously across all identified systems to eliminate attacker footholds in a single window, preventing the adversary from pivoting or retaliating.
- Control Validation & Remediation Verification: Validates that implemented security mitigations effectively block recurrence before reintroducing affected hosts into the enterprise production network.

provenance.title: PwC Incident Management, Digital Forensics & Crisis Remediation Framework

title: KPMG Cyber Response Framework & Continuous Threat Monitoring
text:
KPMG Cyber Response Framework Summary.
Source URL: https://kpmg.com/xx/en/home/services/advisory/risk-consulting/cyber-security/incident-response.html

Paraphrased Architecture Notes:
- Continuous Defense Monitoring & Signal Correlation: Advocates continuous correlation of perimeter sensor logs and host telemetry. Treats low-severity signals (such as port sweeps and repeated login errors) as early warning precursors to multi-stage intrusions.
- Threat Modeling & Attack Path Analysis: Employs threat path graphs to model likely attacker advancement vectors from initial foothold to core database and identity assets, allowing targeted pre-emptive blocking of lateral choke points.
- Automated Orchestration & Playbook Execution: Standardizes response actions via verified orchestration playbooks to reduce analyst mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) while retaining human authorization for disruptive isolation actions.
- Post-Incident Resilience & Continuous Posture Enhancement: Converts incident post-mortems into quantifiable security architecture improvements, verifying that defensive rules and segmentation controls are hardened against similar threat vectors.

provenance.title: KPMG Cyber Response Framework & Continuous Threat Monitoring
